● Collect → Feedback flows in from multiple sources
● Synthesize → ClientQ translates to JTBD statements

● Archive → Learnings go into institutional memory
Every feedback becomes a data point. Every pattern becomes a testable hypothesis. Every hypothesis becomes organizational knowledge.

sourceExcerpt: Build a Metrics Ladder
The metrics ladder connects the why, what, and how of measurement.
Here's how it works:
Top of the ladder: Business Value
What's the strategic outcome we're working toward?
Examples:
● Increase annual recurring revenue by 30%
● Reduce customer acquisition cost by 20%
● Improve net retention to 110%
Middle of the ladder: Customer Value
What behavior change or outcome matters to the user that will drive that business value?
Examples:
● Users complete their first successful action within 3 days
● Teams collaborate on projects 3x per week (up from 1x)
● Users invite colleagues to join (viral coefficient >1.2)
Bottom of the ladder: Traction Metrics
What can the team measure in a sprint to know they're making progress?

sourceExcerpt: What a Learning Plan Actually Is
Think of it as a decision rehearsal—you're planning your next moves before you know the results.
It's not a template you fill out to satisfy the process. It's a thinking tool that forces clarity about:
● What we believe will happen (hypothesis)
● How we'll know if we're right (metrics)
● What we'll do if we're wrong (pivot options)
● What we'll learn either way (capture mechanism)
When done right, a Learning Plan turns every experiment into an institutional asset, not just a one-time test.
The Ten Components
Here's what goes into a solid Learning Plan:
1. Business Problem / Customer Outcome
Start here. Not with the feature. Not with the shiny idea. But with the why.
Ask:
● What business goal are we serving? (Revenue? Retention? Acquisition?)

sourceExcerpt: Anchor Roadmaps in Customer Outcomes
Most roadmaps start with features.
Great ones start with jobs-to-be-done and customer outcomes.
This is where Outcome-Driven Innovation (Ulwick) becomes your north star.
Instead of:
Q3 Roadmap:
● Rebuild notification system
● Add team collaboration features
● Improve dashboard performance
Try:
Q3 Learning Goals:
● Reduce overwhelm: Help users filter signal from noise (Target: 40% reduction in "mute all notifications" actions)
● Enable coordination: Let teams work together without friction (Target: 30% increase in multi-person file edits)
● Increase confidence: Give users trust in real-time data (Target: Dashboard refresh rate <5 seconds)
Now your roadmap isn't a timeline of tech debt and business asks—it's a story of progress toward real impact.

sourceExcerpt: What ClientQ Actually Does
Whether you feed it one quote or a spreadsheet full of comments, ClientQ:
1. Ingests raw feedback
Surveys, transcripts, tickets, NPS comments—anything textual
2. Extracts job steps and desired outcomes
Translates "this is confusing" into "minimize time spent understanding how to X"
3. Sorts outcomes by type
● Minimize (reduce time, effort, risk)
● Increase (improve quality, confidence, speed)
● Enable (make something possible)
● Reduce (lower cost, complexity, anxiety)
4. Optionally scores by importance and satisfaction
If you provide data, it can prioritize the biggest gaps
5. Outputs structured JTBD statements
Ready for your hypothesis backlog, roadmap discussions, or test designs
And it does it in minutes—not days.

sourceExcerpt: The Tools: VisionScope + MarketCraft
These tools don't just clean your pitch. They simulate what your future story will sound like—across the org, and in the wild.
VisionScope — Your Early-Stage Articulation Engine
Think of it like this:
"If this were launching next quarter, how would we talk about it?"
VisionScope helps you:
● Write the press release before you write the PRD
● Articulate the "why this, why now" in compelling language
● Generate FAQs that surface objections you haven't thought of
● Draft vision narratives that align internal teams
● Test whether your idea is inspiring or just jargon
MarketCraft — Your Go-to-Market Pressure Tester
Think of it as your virtual GTM war room—but faster, cheaper, and friendlier.
MarketCraft helps you:
● Simulate stakeholder reactions (customers, competitors, analysts)
● Test positioning across different segments
